stem: A bank wants to find fraud rings, where accounts are linked through shared phone numbers, devices and addresses, often several links apart. Which type of data store is designed for this kind of query?

choices.text: An object store, which keeps each account's history as a file that is downloaded and read as a single whole object.
A key-value database, which returns a single value very quickly when the application already knows its exact key.
A column-family database, which groups related columns together so that very wide rows can be scanned quickly.
A graph database, which stores entities as nodes and the relationships between them as edges that queries traverse.

stem: An order system must record an order, reduce stock and charge the customer as one unit that either completes fully or not at all, and staff run ad hoc queries that join orders with customers. Which kind of data store fits best?

choices.text: An object store, because each order can be saved as one file and the files can be joined to other files with SQL.
A relational database, which enforces a schema, supports multi-row transactions and runs SQL queries with joins.
A graph database, because each order is a relationship between a customer and products that queries can traverse.
A key-value store, because single-key reads and writes are atomic and so they cover changes that span several records.

stem: A real-estate website must store millions of property photos and virtual-tour videos and serve them to browsers. The files are written once and rarely change. Which Azure service is designed for this kind of data?

choices.text: Azure Managed Redis, an in-memory key-value store that holds each photo in memory for very fast repeated reads.
Azure Blob Storage, an object store for unstructured data such as images, videos, documents and backup files.
Azure Database for PostgreSQL, a relational service that stores the media as table rows next to the listing data.
Azure SQL Database, storing each photo and video in a table column so that the database manages the large files.

stem: A new team member hears the term "NoSQL database" and asks what it means. Which TWO statements about nonrelational (NoSQL) databases are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: They require every record to have exactly the same fields, which the database checks on every write.
They store data only as tables of rows that reference one another through primary and foreign keys.
None of them can ever be queried with any SQL-like language, which is where the NoSQL name comes from.
Some of them support a variant of the SQL language, even though they are called NoSQL databases.
They are data management systems that do not apply a relational schema to the data they store.

stem: A legacy mainframe exports customer data as plain text with no commas or tabs. Every name takes exactly 20 characters, padded with spaces, and every date takes 8. A new tool that splits lines on commas returns each line as one field. What format is the export?

choices.text: Fixed-width text, a delimited-text variant in which each field is given a fixed number of characters.
XML, a tagged text format in which each field is padded to a set length inside its own element tags.
Parquet, a columnar binary format that stores each field in a column chunk with a fixed byte length.
Avro, a binary row-based format whose JSON header tells the tool the length of each field in every record.

stem: A media company needs to store millions of product photos and short videos and serve them directly to web browsers over HTTPS. The files have no fixed schema. Which Azure storage service is designed for this?

choices.text: Azure Files, which stores the photos in an SMB file share that each web browser mounts as a network drive before viewing.
Azure Table storage, which stores each photo and video as an entity with a partition key and a row key for fast lookups.
Azure Blob Storage, which stores large amounts of unstructured data as objects that clients reach by URL over HTTP or HTTPS.
Azure SQL Database, which stores each photo and video in a table column so the website can query them with Transact-SQL.

stem: A developer is learning how Azure Blob Storage organizes data. Which statement correctly describes the relationship between a storage account, a container and a blob?

choices.text: A container holds one or more storage accounts, and each storage account holds the blobs for a single application.
A blob holds one or more containers, and each container stores one file together with its metadata and properties.
A storage account holds exactly one container, and that container must hold blobs of only one blob type at a time.
A storage account holds containers, and each container organizes a set of blobs, much like a folder holds files.

stem: A team will store three kinds of data in Azure Blob Storage: uploaded PDF documents, an application log that only ever has new lines added to its end, and the virtual hard disk of a VM that needs fast random reads and writes. Which blob type matches each?

choices.text: Page blobs for the PDFs, block blobs for the log file, and append blobs for the VM disk that is read and written at random.
Block blobs for the PDFs, append blobs for the log file, and page blobs for the VM disk that is read and written at random.
Block blobs for all three, because the blob type is chosen automatically by Azure from the file extension during upload.
Append blobs for the PDFs, page blobs for the log file, and block blobs for the VM disk that is read and written at random.

stem: An application writes audit events to an append blob. A developer now tries to correct an event that was written an hour ago by overwriting that part of the blob, and the operation is not supported. Why?

choices.text: Append blobs can only be changed by an administrator who has a lease on the container, so the developer needs the container lease first.
Append blobs are stored in the archive tier by default, so the blob must be rehydrated to an online tier before any part is changed.
Append blobs only allow new blocks to be added at the end, and updating or deleting existing blocks is not supported for this blob type.
Append blobs are read-only once they reach 1 MB in size, so any older event becomes locked until the blob is copied to a new block blob.

stem: A retailer keeps its product images in Azure Blob Storage. The images are viewed thousands of times a day by the online store. Which access tier gives the lowest access cost for this data?

choices.text: Hot tier, because it is the online tier for data in active use, with the highest storage cost but the lowest access cost.
Cool tier, because it has lower storage costs than hot and is meant for data that the store reads many times every day.
Cold tier, because it has the lowest access cost of the online tiers when data is read thousands of times every day.
Archive tier, because it has the lowest storage cost and still lets the store read each image immediately when needed.

stem: A company keeps monthly reports in Azure Blob Storage. After a few months, reports are opened only a few times a year, but when someone asks for one it must open immediately. The company wants to cut storage cost. Which tier fits best?

choices.text: Hot tier, because older data accessed only a few times a year costs the least to store when it stays in the hot tier.
Cold tier, because it is an online tier for rarely accessed data that still needs fast retrieval, at a lower storage cost.
Archive tier, because it is the cheapest tier and it returns each report within a few seconds whenever a user requests it.
Premium block blob performance, because SSD-based storage has the lowest storage cost for data that is rarely accessed.

stem: An analyst tries to download a two-year-old backup file from Azure Blob Storage and gets an error saying the blob can't be read. The blob's access tier shows Archive. What must happen before the file can be downloaded?

choices.text: The blob must be converted from a block blob to a page blob, because only page blobs can be downloaded once they are archived.
The storage account's redundancy must be changed to zone-redundant storage, because archived blobs are only readable from ZRS.
The blob must be rehydrated to an online tier such as hot, cool or cold, which can take several hours depending on the priority.
The analyst must be given access to the blob's container again, because archived blobs lose all permissions after 180 days.

stem: A company stores invoice scans in Azure Blob Storage. Scans should move to the cool tier 30 days after they were last modified and to archive after 180 days, without anyone moving them by hand. What should the company use?

choices.text: Azure Table storage, which records the age of each blob in an entity and moves the blob when its row key value has expired.
The default account access tier, which moves every blob one tier cooler on its own each time 30 days pass since its last change.
Azure Files snapshots, which copy each blob to a cooler file share automatically on the schedule that the administrator defines.
A lifecycle management policy, a set of rules that moves blobs to cooler tiers or deletes them based on conditions such as age.

stem: A team reviews the characteristics of the Azure Blob Storage archive tier before using it for compliance records. Which TWO statements are true? (Select TWO)

choices.text: It is offline, so a blob must be rehydrated to an online tier before its content can be read again.
It is an online tier, so archived blobs can be read immediately but at a slightly higher access cost.
It can be set as the default access tier of a storage account so that all new uploads are archived.
It can be applied to page blobs and append blobs as well as to block blobs in the same container.
It has the lowest storage cost of the access tiers, in exchange for higher retrieval costs and latency.

stem: An administrator tries to move a large application log, stored as an append blob, to the cool tier to save money. Moving the PDF files in the same container worked, but the log's tier can't be set. What is the reason?

choices.text: The cool tier requires data to stay for at least 90 days, and the append blob was created less than 90 days ago.
The container's public access level must be changed to private before any append blob in it can be moved to cool.
Append blobs can be moved only to the archive tier, so the log must go straight to archive instead of to the cool tier.
Access tiers can be set only on block blobs; append blobs and page blobs don't support hot, cool, cold or archive.

stem: A data team wants Azure Data Lake Storage capabilities for a new analytics project. What do they need to do to get them?

choices.text: Create an Azure Table storage table with a partition key per folder, because Data Lake Storage is built on tables.
Enable the hierarchical namespace setting on an Azure Storage account, so its Blob Storage gains data lake features.
Create a separate Azure Data Lake Storage service resource that is unrelated to Blob Storage and has its own APIs.
Create an Azure file share that uses the NFS protocol, because Data Lake Storage is a feature of Azure Files shares.

stem: A data engineering team stores raw sales files in a storage account and organizes them into folders by year and month. Which TWO benefits do they gain by enabling the hierarchical namespace? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The files become rows in a relational table, so the team can join them to other tables with foreign key constraints.
Every file is automatically converted to Parquet format, so analytics engines can read it without any extra steps.
Permissions can be set on individual directories and files with POSIX access control lists as well as Azure RBAC.
The files no longer count toward storage costs, because directory data is billed only when it is read by a query.
Renaming or deleting a whole directory becomes a single atomic metadata operation instead of a change to every blob.

stem: A company plans to analyze petabytes of raw log and sensor files with Apache Spark. The files must be organized into directories and read through the Hadoop-compatible ABFS driver. Which storage option should they choose?

choices.text: Azure Data Lake Storage, a storage account with the hierarchical namespace enabled, built for big data analytics.
Azure Table storage, because a schemaless key-attribute store lets Apache Spark read each sensor file as a single entity.
Azure Blob Storage with a flat namespace, because name prefixes already give atomic directory renames for Spark jobs.
Azure Files with SMB shares, because SMB is the protocol that Apache Spark uses when it reads files through ABFS.

stem: A company is moving an on-premises Windows file server to Azure. Several Windows and Linux VMs, plus office PCs, must keep mapping the same share at the same time, and the line-of-business app can't be changed. Which service fits?

choices.text: Azure Data Lake Storage, because the hierarchical namespace lets Windows PCs map its directories over SMB by default.
Azure Files, a fully managed file share that clients mount concurrently over SMB from the cloud and on-premises.
Azure Table storage, because each file can be saved as an entity and read by the application using its row key value.
Azure Blob Storage, because each VM can mount a blob container as a Windows drive letter by using the REST API only.

stem: A team compares the two protocols that Azure Files offers for file shares. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Azure Files supports only the NFS protocol, while SMB shares require a Windows Server VM that runs the file server role.
NFS file shares are the usual choice for Windows desktop users, because Windows mounts them as drive letters by default.
A single Azure file share can expose both SMB and NFS at the same time, so mixed clients can share one set of files.
NFS file shares are intended for Linux clients and workloads, such as containers and high-performance computing (HPC).
SMB file shares can be mounted by Windows, Linux and macOS clients, and are the usual choice to replace Windows file servers.

stem: A company moved its file shares to Azure Files, but branch offices with slow internet links still want fast local access to frequently used files from an on-premises Windows Server. What can provide this?

choices.text: Azure File Sync, which caches Azure file shares on on-premises Windows Servers so frequently used files are read locally.
Azure Data Lake Storage, which copies the hierarchical namespace to each branch so that users read directories locally.
Azure Table storage replication, which keeps a copy of each file's entity on every branch server for local access.
A lifecycle management policy, which moves frequently used files from Azure Files to a server in each branch office.

stem: A developer is choosing where to keep app data and reads about Azure Table storage for the first time. Which statement best describes this service?

choices.text: An object store for large unstructured files such as images and video, organized into containers inside a storage account.
A managed file share service that clients mount over SMB or NFS to store documents in a shared hierarchy of folders.
A NoSQL key-attribute store for structured, non-relational data, where a table doesn't enforce a schema on its entities.
A relational database service that enforces a fixed schema on each table and supports foreign keys and stored procedures.

stem: An app stores customer orders as entities in Azure Table storage, using CustomerId as the partition key and OrderId as the row key. Which TWO statements about these keys are true? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The row key uniquely identifies an entity within its partition, so the partition key plus row key identify one entity.
The row key decides which properties each entity must have, so every order in the table has exactly the same columns.
Partition keys are optional, so an entity can be saved with only a row key and a timestamp to identify it in the table.
The partition key must be a foreign key that refers to a row in another table, which keeps the orders linked to customers.
Entities that share the same partition key can be queried more quickly and can be inserted or updated in atomic operations.

stem: A web app stores user preferences and device settings. Each record is looked up by a known key, records vary in their fields, and no joins or stored procedures are needed. The team wants the lowest-cost option. Which service fits?

choices.text: Azure SQL Database, because a relational schema with joins is the cheapest way to store records that have changing fields.
Azure Table storage, a low-cost schemaless key-attribute store for structured data that doesn't need joins or foreign keys.
Azure Files, because storing each user's settings as a file on an SMB share gives the fastest lookups by key at low cost.
Azure Blob Storage archive tier, because it has the lowest storage cost and returns small records instantly by their key.

stem: A new employee asks how the core Azure Storage services differ. Which pairing of service and typical use is correct?

choices.text: Blob Storage for key-attribute app data, Azure Files for images and video, and Table storage for SMB shares mapped by PCs.
Blob Storage for images and video, Azure Files for key-attribute app data, and Table storage for SMB shares mapped by PCs.
Blob Storage for images and video, Azure Files for SMB shares mapped by PCs, and Table storage for key-attribute app data.
Blob Storage for SMB shares mapped by PCs, Azure Files for key-attribute app data, and Table storage for images and video.

stem: An online retailer has shoppers on four continents. Its shopping-cart service stores JSON data whose shape changes often, and every shopper must get fast reads and writes from a nearby region. Which Azure data service fits best?

choices.text: Azure Blob Storage, with each shopping cart saved as a separate JSON file in a container in one region.
Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server, with one server in one region and JSON stored in columns.
Azure SQL Database, with one database in a central region and a fixed table schema for every cart row.
Azure Cosmos DB, with the account replicated to several Azure regions and multi-region writes turned on.

stem: A company already uses Azure Cosmos DB for its mobile app. It now wants interactive dashboards and large batch analysis over years of sales history for its data analysts. What does Microsoft recommend for this analytical workload?

choices.text: Running the analysts' large aggregate queries directly against the app's Cosmos DB containers during business hours.
Creating a second Cosmos DB account with the Apache Gremlin API, because graph queries are designed for sales reporting.
Moving all of the app's data into Azure Table storage, because a key-value store is designed for analytical queries.
Mirroring the Cosmos DB data into Microsoft Fabric and running the analysts' dashboards and batch analysis there.

stem: A developer is starting a new app on Azure Cosmos DB and wants the native API, which stores JSON documents and is queried with a SQL-like syntax. Which API is it?

choices.text: Azure Cosmos DB for Table, which stores rows that are found by a partition key and a row key.
Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL, the API that older documentation and samples refer to as the SQL API.
Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB, which stores BSON documents queried with the MongoDB Query Language.
Azure Cosmos DB for Apache Cassandra, which stores column-family tables queried with CQL statements.

stem: A development team has years of experience with MongoDB drivers and the MongoDB Query Language. It wants to keep using them while gaining the request-unit-based, globally distributed Cosmos DB model. Which Azure Cosmos DB API should it choose?

choices.text: Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB, which supports the MongoDB wire protocol and stores data in BSON format.
Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL, which stores JSON documents but needs the Cosmos DB SDKs and SQL-like queries.
Azure Cosmos DB for Table, which stores entities and is queried through Azure Table storage SDK calls.
Azure Cosmos DB for Apache Gremlin, which stores vertices and edges and is queried by graph traversals.

stem: A social networking startup stores people, the groups they join and who follows whom. Its most important queries walk these relationships, such as "friends of friends who like this band". Which Azure Cosmos DB API fits this data best?

choices.text: Azure Cosmos DB for Apache Cassandra, storing each person as a row in a column-family table.
Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB, storing each person as a BSON document in a single collection.
Azure Cosmos DB for Apache Gremlin, storing people as vertices and relationships as edges.
Azure Cosmos DB for Table, storing each person as an entity with a partition key and a row key.

stem: A company runs an Apache Cassandra cluster for sensor readings and its developers write Cassandra Query Language (CQL). It wants a fully managed Azure Cosmos DB API that keeps its Cassandra drivers and CQL statements. Which API should it use?

choices.text: Azure Cosmos DB for Apache Gremlin, loading each sensor as a vertex and each reading as an edge.
Azure Cosmos DB for Apache Cassandra, which supports CQL and works with existing Cassandra drivers.
Azure Cosmos DB for Table, loading every reading as a key-value entity with a partition and row key.
Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL, rewriting each CQL statement as a SQL-like query over JSON documents.

stem: An app stores device registrations in Azure Table storage. The company now needs its key-value data replicated to several regions and indexed on every property, with minimal code changes. Which option does Learn suggest?

choices.text: Moving the data to Azure SQL Database, which stores each device as a row in a normalized relational table.
Moving the data to Azure Cosmos DB for Apache Gremlin, which stores each device as a vertex in a graph.
Moving the data to Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, which stores each device as a file in a folder tree.
Moving the data to Azure Cosmos DB for Table, which uses the same programming model as Table storage.

stem: In the Azure Cosmos DB resource hierarchy, at which level do you set the partition key, the throughput and the indexing policy for a set of items?

choices.text: The container, which is the primary unit of storage and scaling where these settings are configured.
The database, which is a logical namespace and sets one indexing policy shared by all of its items.
The item, which is a single document, row, node or edge and carries its own throughput settings.
The account, which is the top-level Azure resource and sets one partition key for all of its databases.

stem: In one Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL container, one item has five properties and another item has fifteen completely different properties. Which characteristic of Cosmos DB does this show?

choices.text: Table normalization, because the extra properties are split automatically into separate linked tables.
Column-family storage, because the native API stores every property as its own column on disk storage.
Schema-agnostic storage, because items in the same container do not need to share the same structure.
Strict schema enforcement, because the container rejects items whose properties differ from the first item.

stem: Developers moving from a relational database to Azure Cosmos DB ask how indexes are created for the properties their queries filter on. What is the default behavior?

choices.text: Cosmos DB automatically creates and maintains indexes on all item properties, with no manual index management.
Cosmos DB indexes only the item id property, so every other filter performs a full scan of the container.
Cosmos DB creates no indexes until a database administrator runs a CREATE INDEX statement for each property.
Cosmos DB builds indexes once per night in a batch job, so new items are not searchable until the next day.

stem: A team is choosing a partition key for a Cosmos DB container of customer orders that will grow large. Which choice follows the guidance on Learn?

choices.text: A property that changes on every update, such as `lastModified`, so that new writes always go to new partitions.
A property with many distinct values and an even spread of data, such as `customerId`, to balance throughput.
A property with only two values, such as `isPriority`, so that the data stays in as few partitions as possible.
A property that is the same for every item, such as `country` in a one-country shop, so all orders stay together.

stem: A multiplayer game stores player profiles in Azure Cosmos DB. Players in Europe and Asia complain that saving their progress is slow, because every write goes to the single write region in the US. Which feature addresses this?

choices.text: Moving the profiles to a serverless account, so that each save is billed only for the RUs it consumes.
Changing the container's indexing policy, so that fewer properties are indexed when a profile is saved.
Switching the account to the Strong consistency level, so that each save is confirmed by every region.
Enabling multi-region writes, so that each player writes to the nearest region and data is replicated.

stem: A banking app on Azure Cosmos DB must never show a balance that is older than the latest committed write, even if this adds latency. Which consistency level gives this guarantee?

choices.text: Session, which guarantees consistency only within a single client session that made the write.
Eventual, which lets replicas converge over time and gives the weakest guarantee of the levels.
Strong, which guarantees that every read reflects the most recent committed write to the data.
Consistent prefix, which never shows writes out of order but may still return some stale data.

stem: In a shopping app, each user must always see the items they just added to their own cart, while it is fine if other users see changes a little later. Which consistency level does this describe, the one Learn calls the most widely used?

choices.text: Session, which guarantees that within a client session the user reads the writes made in that session.
Eventual, which gives no ordering guarantee, so a user may not see their own newest change at once.
Strong, which makes every read in every region wait until the latest write is committed everywhere.
Bounded staleness, which lets all reads lag behind writes by a set time or number of item versions.

stem: Azure Cosmos DB measures and bills database capacity in request units (RUs). Which statement describes a request unit correctly?

choices.text: The number of virtual CPU cores assigned to the account, chosen from a list of sizes when the account is created.
A single performance currency for all operations, roughly the cost of reading one 1-KB item by its ID and partition key.
A fixed hourly fee for each container, charged the same amount no matter how many reads and writes it handles.
A count of client connections that may be open at once, after which further requests are queued by the service.

stem: A small team is building an internal tool on Azure Cosmos DB. Traffic is intermittent and hard to predict, there are hours with no requests, and the tool runs in one Azure region. Which throughput option fits best?

choices.text: Dedicated provisioned throughput on each container, reserving a fixed number of RU/s around the clock.
Shared provisioned throughput at database level, reserving RU/s that up to 25 containers can share.
Multi-region writes with provisioned throughput, so idle capacity in one region serves the others.
Serverless, with no throughput to provision upfront and billing only for the RUs requests consume.

stem: A ticket-booking site on Azure Cosmos DB is usually quiet but gets sudden traffic bursts when popular concerts go on sale. It must run in several regions. Which throughput setting lets capacity follow demand automatically?

choices.text: Serverless, because serverless accounts can be replicated to any number of Azure regions for bursts.
Manual provisioned throughput, where an operator resizes the RU/s by hand whenever a sale is announced.
Autoscale provisioned throughput, where you set a maximum RU/s and Cosmos DB scales within that range.
Shared database throughput, where every container of the database permanently gets the same fixed RU/s.

stem: An architect reads about Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL while planning a new distributed relational app. Which statement reflects its status on Learn?

choices.text: It is the native Cosmos DB API that stores JSON documents and is the recommended default for new projects.
It is a distributed PostgreSQL service with Citus that is on a retirement path and not recommended for new projects.
It is a key-value API that uses the same programming model and SDKs as Azure Table storage for its entities.
It is a graph API built on Apache TinkerPop that the PostgreSQL engine uses to store vertices and edges.

stem: Which TWO statements describe Azure Cosmos DB correctly? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Each account can hold only one container, so every new set of data needs a separate Cosmos DB account.
You install the Cosmos DB engine on your own virtual machines and apply its monthly updates yourself.
You can add Azure regions to an account at any time, and Cosmos DB replicates the data to them automatically.
You must define a fixed table schema for each container before the first item can be inserted into it.
It is a fully managed PaaS service, so Microsoft handles server provisioning, patching, updates and backups.

stem: Which TWO Azure Cosmos DB APIs use a query language with a syntax similar to SQL? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Azure Cosmos DB for Apache Cassandra, queried with CQL statements such as SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE ID = 2.
Azure Cosmos DB for Table, queried through REST-style addresses such as Customers(PartitionKey='1',RowKey='124').
Azure Cosmos DB for Apache Gremlin, queried with traversals such as g.V().hasLabel('employee').order().by('id').
Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB, queried with method calls on collections such as db.products.find({id: 123}).
Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL, queried with statements such as SELECT * FROM customers c WHERE c.id = "joe".

stem: Which TWO workloads does Learn list as good fits for Azure Cosmos DB? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A highly relational line-of-business app whose reports depend on complex joins across many tables.
Long-term archiving of large video files that are read rarely and must be kept at the lowest cost.
An enterprise data warehouse for interactive and batch analytics by data analysts over years of history.
Player profiles, leaderboards and in-game stats for a game that needs low-latency reads and writes.
Fast ingestion of high-frequency IoT device telemetry that is made available for near-real-time processing.

stem: Which TWO statements about choosing an API in Azure Cosmos DB are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Each container in an account can use a different API, so one account can mix MongoDB, Cassandra and Gremlin data.
The API is chosen per query, so the same container can answer SQL-like, CQL and Gremlin requests side by side.
Internally Cosmos DB stores data in its own format, and the API is an abstraction layer on top of that storage.
Each API runs the original open-source database product on servers that you size, patch and upgrade yourself.
You choose the API when you create the account, and it decides the data format, query language and client libraries.

stem: A credit card company sends each customer one bill a month that lists all of that month's purchases, instead of a bill after every purchase. Which kind of data processing does this describe?

choices.text: Transactional processing, because each purchase is written to the database as a separate atomic operation.
Stream processing, because each purchase is read as an event the moment the card is swiped at the shop.
Real-time processing, because the billing system watches the purchase feed and reacts within a few seconds.
Batch processing, because the month's purchases are collected and stored, then processed together in one run.

stem: A building management system monitors smoke and heat sensors. When readings show a fire, it must sound alarms and unlock exit doors immediately. Which processing approach fits this requirement?

choices.text: Stream processing that evaluates every sensor reading as it arrives and triggers the alarm as soon as it matches.
Batch processing triggered when enough sensor readings have accumulated in a file in the building's data lake.
Batch processing that collects the sensor readings every hour and runs a job that checks them for fire patterns.
A nightly data warehouse load that keeps a full history of sensor readings for analysis by the facilities team.

stem: Which TWO statements correctly describe stream processing compared with batch processing? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Stream processing requires all input data to be fully prepared and validated before any processing can begin.
Stream processing typically produces results within seconds or milliseconds of the data being received.
Stream processing is mainly used for complex analytics that must read every record in the full historical dataset.
Stream processing typically has latency of a few hours, because events are buffered until a scheduled run.
Stream processing typically works on the most recent data or on a rolling time window, such as the last 30 seconds.

stem: A city traffic department wants a live dashboard of cars passing each sensor per minute, and also wants to analyze traffic volumes over the past year. What is the common way to meet both needs?

choices.text: Process the stream for the live dashboard and also persist the results in an analytical store for historical analysis.
